record.context_brief: Lattice-strictly singular versus disjointly strictly singular
record.original_question: Does there exist an operator T from a Banach lattice X into a Banach space Y that is lattice-strictly singular but not disjointly strictly singular? Here T is lattice-strictly singular if it is not an isomorphism on any sublattice of X, and it is disjointly strictly singular if it is not an isomorphism on any subspace of X spanned by a disjoint sequence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach lattice and $Y$ a Banach space. A bounded linear operator $T : X \to Y$ is called:
(i) lattice-strictly singular if the restriction of $T$ to any infinite-dimensional sublattice of $X$ fails to be an isomorphism onto its image;
(ii) disjointly strictly singular if the restriction of $T$ to the closed linear span of any pairwise disjoint sequence in $X$ fails to be an isomorphism onto its image.

Every disjointly strictly singular operator is lattice-strictly singular. The problem is: does there exist a Banach lattice $X$, a Banach space $Y$, and a bounded linear operator $T : X \to Y$ that is lattice-strictly singular but not disjointly strictly singular? Equivalently, do these two classes of operators coincide?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the classes of lattice-strictly singular (LSS) and disjointly strictly singular (DSS) operators coincide appears to remain open. Partial results are known: super-LSS coincides with super-DSS, and LSS equals DSS in certain stable Banach lattice settings, but no general resolution has been published.

status_evidence.title: Strict Singularity: A Lattice Approach
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses LSS vs DSS classes and partial coincidence results.
status_evidence.claim: A survey/chapter still discussing the relationship as not fully resolved, with partial results.

status_evidence.title: Banach lattice versions of strict singularity
status_evidence.snippet: Studies LSS and DSS operators, showing equivalence under additional hypotheses such as stability.
status_evidence.claim: LSS = DSS proved only under additional assumptions, suggesting the general question remains open.
